trap.segment: Vegans and strict vegetarians: 72% purchase intent but only 1.3 million adults, 2.5% of adults 18-64

items.quote: This is the largest segment, 17.5M adults (34% of adults aged 18-64), with 41% purchase intent.
Vegans show 72% intent but number only 1.3M, too few for the volume goals.

The French protein snack category was worth 480M euros in 2024 and grew 11% per year from 2021 to 2024; plant-based products are 18% of it, and 27% of French adults bought a protein snack in the last three months [1].
It sits inside a 2.9 billion euro savoury snack market [1].
Supermarkets and hypermarkets make up 68% of protein snack sales, specialised sport and organic shops 17%, online 9%, and gyms and vending 6% [1].
Trade press reports that protein-enriched products on shelves grew 86% between 2021 and 2025 [3].
Private labels are 35.7% of food sales value and are priced 30-35% below equivalent national brands on average [4].
Its almond sport and nutrition bar has 7.9 g protein and 57 g sugars per 100 g [10].
Barebells prices found are from non-supermarket online retailers (Primor, about 2.25-2.29 euros per 55 g bar [8]; Idealo, a 12-bar pack from 26.16 euros, about 2.18 per bar [9]).

sources.reference: Document: Company document, section 3 (Why France, and launch goals)

strategy_vs_analysis.reason: The target SEG2 is chosen on the analysis's size and interest figures (17.5M adults, 41% intent versus SEG1 at 1.3M and 72%), and the rationale compares all four segments against the volume goals. Channels follow the accessibility figures (supermarkets 68%, gyms 6%), and the positioning answers the Barebells and private-label competition. Pricing is handled explicitly: no price war with private labels, a premium to private labels, and a shelf-price audit before fixing the price.

campaign_vs_strategy.reason: Every message ("Côté salé", the sporty-routine framing, gym bag and post-session moments) speaks to active adults and carries the positioning proof points (15 g per 40 g, six ingredients, Nutri-Score A on two flavours). The channel-specific messages use only the five strategy channels (supermarkets, gyms and sport shops, organic shops, online shop, Instagram), and the vegan angle appears only in claims about certification, not as a separate target.
